implementation.cause: Old accept_snapshot restarted its physical-interval blend from the most recently DRAWN body/environment/striker pose and time. Multiple accepted replies before a draw could repeatedly rebase from stale displayed state, accumulating presentation lag.
implementation.fix: Shared PresentationClock samples the OLD active blend at the new arrival before replacing interval/target/arrival. New interval still comes from consecutive physical target times. One old f32 alpha rebases body,environment,striker and f64 presentation time. Displayed/picking caches remain unchanged during acceptance and update on draw. One snap policy covers first/new generation,pause,discontinuity,geometry/presence change and nonpositive target delta.
implementation.limits: Clamped interpolation between observed endpoints only, no physical extrapolation or worker mutation. Explicit reset/discontinuity snap remains a presentation response to the existing physical snapshot. Before-first-draw caches, generation-change camera transition and pre-submit cache updates on failed draw are documented nonblocking caveats below.

caveats: Before the first draw, submitted pose caches remain zero/empty; normal app and all actual-app harnesses wait for drawn frames. Picking/focus guards for frames==0 are a possible future cleanup.
Generation changes can update camera/geometry before the next draw; the ordinary acceptance picking-cache guarantee is scoped to unchanged geometry/camera.
Draw still writes displayed caches before texture acquisition/submit. A failed draw could expose an unsubmitted pose; this pre-existing failed-draw behavior was not expanded into this narrow fix.
